about: The machine-checkable half of the dataset contract (INTERFACE.md §2.5.9, §8.1).
It is read by tools/dataset_lint.py, which the quality suite runs, and by
tools/datasets.py, which renders DOWNLOADS.md from the same loaders.
It deliberately holds only what can be decided without judgement: names, shapes,
coverage, path spelling, and the pinning of a download. Everything that needs a
human -- 'is this trap real?', 'does this goal leak the answer?' -- lives in
docs/dataset-onboarding-skill.md instead, because a rule that cannot be evaluated
by a program is a rule that trains people to ignore the check.

oracle_about: Gate 1 is the oracle control: the dataset's own reference artifact, submitted, expected to score 1. Until 2026-10-08 that artifact was always the benchmark's released answer, so nothing had to say so; the owner then authorised platform-authored references validated by the released tests, and the two are different claims about a curve. Silence is refused rather than defaulted, the rule OFFICIAL_EVAL already follows.

`released`: the reference comes from the benchmark's own release (a gold answer, a walkthrough, a gold SQL). `authored`: the platform wrote it, `ORACLE_VALIDATED_BY` names what validates it, and `ORACLE_COVERAGE` says how much of the pool has one -- an authored oracle covering three tasks proves the check is reachable on three tasks, and a reader has to be able to see that.

verify.image: optional pinned verifier image for an exec command; defaults to the task image

paths.why: Code (how to load and score) is in git; data is not. A dataset whose root is inside the platform tree has put bytes into git that the next reader will silently get a different copy of.

platform_tree: the directory containing this file's parent, i.e. the HarnessGrad checkout
